We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have guidance: three steps: (1) amide formation from carboxylic acid + amine (coupling). (2) Doebner modification to form α,β-unsaturated acid from aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid. (3) sulfonamide formation from amine + sulfonyl chloride.

Thus retrosynthetic direction: target -> break amide to give acid and aniline (or amine). The amide is C(=O)N attached to phenyl (c3ccccc3N). Actually the amide is C(=O)N attached to an aniline (Nc3ccccc3N). Wait structure: .../C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N . So the amide carbonyl attached to N which is attached to phenyl with an NH (aniline). So amide formation step: carboxylic acid (the α,β-unsaturated acid) + aniline (with NH2) to give amide.

Thus retrosynthesis step 1: target -> disconnection at amide bond: produce α,β-unsaturated acid (with phenyl attached to N? Actually the amide carbonyl attached to N which is attached to phenyl with an NH2 substituent? The SMILES: C(=O)N c3ccccc3N . That is an amide where the nitrogen is attached to a phenyl that also has an NH (aniline). So the amine component is an aniline with an NH2 (para? Actually c3ccccc3N is an aniline). So the amine is aniline (aniline). So step 1: precursor A: α,β-unsaturated acid (with phenyl ring attached to sulfonamide part) and aniline.

The α,β-unsaturated acid is derived from Doebner modification: aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid. The aldehyde would be the aromatic ring (the second phenyl) bearing sulfonyl group? Actually the unsaturated acid is attached to the sulfonyl phenyl: /C=C/COOH attached to phenyl sulfonyl group. The SMILES: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2 . So the aromatic ring (c2) has side chain /C=C/COOH (actually after amide formation becomes /C=C/C(=O)N...). Wait the unsaturated acid before amide formation would be /C=C/COOH attached to that phenyl. So the aldehyde precursor would be the same phenyl with aldehyde (instead of unsaturated acid). So step 2: aromatic aldehyde (c2ccc(CHO)cc2) + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid (c2ccc(/C=C/COOH)cc2). So we need to identify that aldehyde.

Thus step 2: disconnection at C=C bond formed in Doebner: break to aldehyde and malonic acid.

Step 3: sulfonamide formation: the sulfonamide linking the first phenyl (with methyl) to the second phenyl sulfonyl group. The sulfonamide is formed from sulfonyl chloride (Ar-SO2-Cl) and an amine (the first phenyl with NH). The first phenyl is a tolyl (methyl phenyl) with NH attached to sulfonyl group. So the amine precursor is p-toluidine (4-methyl aniline). The sulfonyl chloride precursor is the sulfonyl chloride derived from the second phenyl (the sulfonyl phenyl). So step 3: disconnection of sulfonamide bond: produce p-toluidine and aryl sulfonyl chloride (Ar-SO2-Cl) where Ar is the second phenyl (the one bearing the unsaturated acid side chain). So we need to propose that.

Thus overall route:

Target (M) -> (1) amide formation: M from α,β-unsaturated acid (A) + aniline (B). (Amide coupling)

A = c2ccc(/C=C/COOH)cc2 (with sulfonyl attached to first phenyl? Wait the sulfonyl is attached to the first phenyl, not the second. Actually the sulfonyl group is attached to the first phenyl (tolyl) and connects to second phenyl. The sulfonamide is between the two phenyls. So the sulfonyl chloride precursor is the second phenyl sulfonyl chloride? Let's parse: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(... )cc2)cc1 . So the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the tolyl ring (c1) and the sulfonyl group attaches to second phenyl (c2). So the sulfonyl chloride precursor would be the second phenyl sulfonyl chloride (Ar-SO2-Cl) where Ar is the second phenyl bearing the side chain (the unsaturated acid after step 1). So step 3: sulfonamide formation between p-toluidine (4-methyl aniline) and aryl sulfonyl chloride (Ar-SO2-Cl) to give sulfonamide.

Thus we need templates for sulfonamide formation (we have template 733 earlier). That template is retro: sulfonamide -> sulfonyl chloride + aniline. Good.

Now we need template for amide formation (carboxylic acid + amine). Search for template that breaks amide to acid + amine. Let's search with functional_groups_broken: ["amide"], functional_groups_formed: ["aliphatic carboxylic acid","primary amines"] maybe.
